decisions.summary: Five passes, five write sessions each followed by a check-and-apply, one queue in one clone
decisions.why: How the work is scheduled; the request does not speak to it and no asked figure depends on it.

decisions.summary: Questions 1 and 2 first, each pair landed on its own, then the reply
decisions.why: The request's Priority line: question 1, then 2, and 3 and 4 may follow.

decisions.summary: No code, map or canon change
decisions.why: The request asks only for the history; the Rokugan decision stays with the GM (also FR-006).

decisions.summary: Passes are leads; each passage is read on its page before citing
decisions.why: Citation method; removes nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Pass C's wrong URLs are not used; the URL comes from make archive-find
decisions.why: Citation hygiene.

decisions.summary: Pass E's three PDFs read by pdftotext and given to the checks by IMAGES= or an archive copy
decisions.why: Tooling route; removes nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Marked drafts cited as such; Nagahara, Ho and Tanimoto cited as read through others; Mazumdar through a blog not cited as Mazumdar
decisions.why: Carries FR-007.

decisions.summary: Nine new questions, at most four questions and ten registry keys per write
decisions.why: Not a narrowing: D1 to D5 name a home for every question the request asks, and FR-001 binds each figure whatever the count. But the number is wrong on the plan's own blocks: D1 (1) + D2 (1) + D3 (2) + D4 (3) + D5 (3) = ten, not nine. The plan should say ten, or name which two are one.

decisions.summary: Performance bookends N/A
decisions.why: No generator change; nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Constitution check: research physical tasks, record checks, built as the FRs
decisions.why: Process; removes nothing asked.

decisions.summary: One Japan cotton question: five stages each with a verdict, what it replaced and how fast, region, class (low-ranking samurai against commoners, sumptuary rules labeled as ceilings), the direct question by region, canon beside it
decisions.why: Clause for clause question 1. Ceilings labeling is FR-005/FR-007 honesty about what the rules show, and answering by region is the fuller answer to a question the request itself asks by region.

decisions.summary: D1 names 0261, 0274, 0312 and 0313 by file; no block names 0209, 0006 or 0020
decisions.why: The request lists six files the record already holds (0261, 0274, 0313, 0209, 0006, 0020) so the session does not redo them, and the accepted spec's User Story 1 scenario 2 requires all six named by file. The plan's only list of them carries three of the six plus 0312, with no reason, and no other block picks up 0209 (dyers and weavers), 0006 or 0020 (dry-field and cash crops on rice land), which sit directly beside D1's commercial-crop stage and D4. Not impossible, not implied by the GM's words, and no purpose is served by the omission. Should say: all six are named by file (0312 in addition), each where it bears.

decisions.summary: One China cotton question of D1's shape, frontier and Yangzi as separate stages, the state's part
decisions.why: Question 1 for China. The frontier/Yangzi split and the state's part serve the by-region and commercial-crop clauses.

decisions.summary: One question on whether cotton was a New World crop: species before 1492, American arrivals, four countries with date and importance, the 100 years answered
decisions.why: Clause for clause question 2's premise check.

decisions.summary: One question on when cotton became ordinary in India and in Korea
decisions.why: The block does not list the stages, but it does not limit them either, and it cites FR-001 while the accepted spec's User Story 1 says the same stages. A one-phrase statement would be clearer; silence here is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Korea's role in CLOTH reaching Japan
decisions.why: The request says 'Korea's role, if any, in cotton reaching Japan', which is the plant and the seed as well as the cloth. D3 replaces the word with the narrower one, and it is a positive statement of the question's content, not a silence. The accepted spec carries a verdict on each: ATTESTED ONLY FOR cloth, and the plant reaching Japan through Korea NOT ATTESTED, the one source naming a seed route saying Ming. As written the plant's verdict has no home, and a NOT ATTESTED the GM would use to weigh the route is dropped. Not impossible, not implied by the request. Should say: Korea's role, if any, in cotton reaching Japan, the cloth and the plant each with its verdict.

decisions.summary: Three questions, one per plant: tobacco, sweet potato, white potato; no question of its own for the native yam
decisions.why: Question 3 asks for cotton's fellow crops and tells the session to keep sweet potato, white potato and native yam apart. The yam is a misidentification to guard against, not a crop whose spread was asked for; the loose-word rule carries it.

decisions.summary: Loose plant words kept as the spec's edge case says
decisions.why: Carries 'say which one each date concerns'.

decisions.summary: Tomato question per country with the lag and the GM's two positions tested
decisions.why: Questions 3 and 4 on the tomato.

decisions.summary: What historians say made a crop spread quickly or slowly, with author and crops
decisions.why: Question 4. The COMPARATIVE mark is not repeated here; the spec's edge case carries it.

decisions.summary: Whether the Tokugawa restrictions stopped new crops, with arrivals before and after
decisions.why: Question 4's last clause. The routes the request names are not restated, and nothing excludes them.

decisions.summary: implementation-check.md holds each new question's line
Reply gives figure by figure the fragment, the verdict and what is open, with the two canon quotations
decisions.why: FR-001 and FR-004; the canon quotations are the request's own.

decisions.summary: Anything for the GM goes through escalation-check; nothing edits the canon
decisions.why: The Rokugan decision stays with the GM.

decisions.summary: make land takes the record's checks; a claims-gate refusal on another feature's Rust claims is taken up when seen
decisions.why: Landing procedure; the request does not reach it and no asked figure depends on it.

decisions.summary: Five write sessions, each with a check-and-apply session, in one sequential queue in this clone; questions 1 and 2 land first; then the reply; no code, map or canon change.
decisions.why: The request orders question 1, then question 2, and lets 3 and 4 follow; it asks only for the history, and the Rokugan decision stays with the GM. One queue against two clones is execution, and all four questions are still worked.

decisions.summary: Passes are leads read on the page; wrong URLs in pass C replaced from make archive-find; pass E's PDFs read by pdftotext; drafts and works read through another cited as such.
decisions.why: Carries FR-007 and the citation rules. None of it removes a figure the request asks for.

decisions.summary: Ten new questions (D1 1, D2 1, D3 2, D4 3, D5 3), each crop its own; a write takes at most four questions and ten registry keys.
decisions.why: The block's own count sums to ten, matching D1-D5. The request says to keep the plants separate. The two caps were checked as real project limits: the 20,000-byte prose cap in research/CLAUDE.md line 79 and the 10-key cap in scripts/pages/page_session_runner.py KEY_CAP, enforced by scripts/record/reserve-prefix.py. A cap decides how the work is divided, not what is answered.

decisions.summary: Performance bookends N/A (no generator change); constitution check limited to XII, XIII and XVI.
decisions.why: The request is research only, so no generator is touched.

decisions.summary: One Japan question: five stages each with a verdict; what cotton replaced and how fast; region and class; the direct question by region; both canon quotations; the six files the request lists each named by file, with 0312 in addition, none repeated.
decisions.why: Round 1's narrowing is gone: all six files the request names are carried (0261, 0274, 0313, 0209, 0006, 0020), matching spec User Story 1 scenario 2, and 0312 only adds. Peasants and townsmen are the request's commoners. Answering the century by region gives each region its century and is what the spec's Japan finding states; the region difference is itself asked for. Who wore it is carried by the class clause.

decisions.summary: One China question of D1's shape, with the frontier and the Yangzi separate and the state's part; points at D1.
decisions.why: Same shape carries the five stages, replacement, region, class, the direct question and the canon. Keeping the frontier and the Yangzi apart serves the request's dated stage 'with place'. The state's part is an addition inside the spec's commercial-crop finding and removes nothing.

decisions.summary: One question on whether cotton was a New World crop: species before 1492, when American kinds came, four countries with date and importance, the GM's 100-year point answered.
decisions.why: Walks request question 2 clause by clause: the premise check, pre-1492 species, American arrival in all four countries, whether they mattered, and the 100 years.

decisions.summary: One question on India and Korea with the same five dated stages as question 1 for each country, and Korea's role, if any, in cotton reaching Japan, the cloth and the plant each with its verdict.
decisions.why: Round 1's narrowing is gone. The request says 'cotton reaching Japan'; the text no longer reduces that to cloth, and each of the two has its own verdict, as the spec's finding does (cloth ATTESTED ONLY FOR, plant NOT ATTESTED). The five stages the request calls for are now stated for each country.

decisions.summary: Three questions, one per plant (tobacco, sweet potato, white potato), each with per-country dated stages and the lag, China and Japan first; loose plant words handled by the spec's edge case; tobacco's canon quotation beside it.
decisions.why: The request says to keep the plants separate. A native yam is named there only as a plant a loose word may mean, not as a crop asked about, so it needs no question of its own; the edge case and User Story 1 scenario 4 keep such a date labeled. China and Japan first is the request's order, and per-country keeps India and Korea.

decisions.summary: Three questions: the tomato per country with the lag and the GM's two positions tested; what historians say set the pace, with author and crops; whether the Tokugawa restrictions stopped new crops, with arrivals before and after.
decisions.why: Carries the tomato part of question 3 and all of question 4. The block does not restrict the routes or the COMPARATIVE marking the request names: 'arrivals' is unqualified, the spec's finding gives the routes (Nagasaki, Tsushima, Ryukyu-Satsuma), and its edge case governs COMPARATIVE. Silence on a point the accepted spec settles is not a decision against it.

decisions.summary: implementation-check.md line per question; the reply gives figure by figure the fragment file, verdict and what is open, including the unread works and each SILENT; both canon quotations stated; anything for the GM through escalation-check; no canon edit.
decisions.why: Carries FR-001, FR-003 and FR-004 and the spec's canon edge case. It leaves the Rokugan decision to the GM as the request says.

decisions.summary: Every delta is a record edit, so make land takes the record's checks; a claims-gate refusal on another feature's owed Rust claims is taken up when seen on a landing.
decisions.why: A landing mechanic. It touches nothing the request asks for.
